templates.title: Reseller application
templates.description: Screen potential resellers on how and where they sell before anyone gets on a call.
templates.metaDescription: Vet would-be resellers before you sign them: business type, markets, sales channels, similar brands they carry and why they want in. Unregistered sellers exit early.
templates.blurb: Built for a partner manager who gets more reseller requests than they can call back. It asks the questions that separate a real sales channel from a curious buyer, stops early for businesses that are not registered yet, and only asks about competing brands when the applicant already sells some.

preview.greeting: Thanks for your interest in reselling with us. This takes about four minutes and helps us reply with something useful.
preview.question: Who should we get back to?
preview.next: What is your business called?

templates.title: Call for speakers
templates.description: Take talk proposals in a shape a review committee can compare at a glance.
templates.metaDescription: Collect conference talk proposals a committee can compare: title, abstract, takeaways, format and bio. Workshops get setup questions, first-timers a mentor offer.
templates.blurb: Proposals tend to arrive as essays when a committee needs a title, an abstract, a length and a bio side by side. This asks for exactly that, then branches: workshop proposals are asked what only a workshop needs, like room setup and what attendees must install, and first-time speakers are offered a mentor.

preview.greeting: Got a talk in you? Tell us about it. Most people finish in about five minutes.
preview.question: Who is proposing the talk?
preview.next: Which pronouns should we use in the programme?

templates.title: Customer information
templates.description: A tidy record for every new customer, whether they buy for themselves or for a business.
templates.metaDescription: Collect a new customer's contact details, address, billing contact and how they like to be reached, with extra questions only for business customers.
templates.blurb: Made for businesses whose customers are mostly people buying for themselves, with the odd company in the mix. It gives your team the record it needs before the first invoice or delivery. Individuals skip straight past the company questions, while business customers are asked for the company name, a tax number and who should receive invoices. It closes by asking how and when they want to hear from you, and records a clear yes or no to marketing.

preview.greeting: Thanks for choosing us. A few details and your account is ready.
preview.question: First, who are you?
preview.next: Are you signing up for yourself or for a business?

templates.title: Booking request
templates.description: Gather everything you need to check availability before you confirm a booking.
templates.metaDescription: Take booking requests for a venue, studio or service with the date, time, group size and extras, plus backup dates so you can confirm without the back-and-forth.
templates.blurb: Built for places that confirm by hand: a venue, studio, rental or service with limited slots. It collects the preferred date and time, how long, how many people and what extras they need. Anyone who says their date is flexible is asked for a second choice straight away, which saves a round of emails when the first date is taken.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell us what you'd like to book and we'll check availability.
preview.question: What's the booking for?

templates.title: Catering inquiry
templates.description: Everything a caterer needs to write a proposal, gathered in one conversation.
templates.metaDescription: Ask about the occasion, date, guest count, venue, service style, dietary needs and budget, so every catering quote you send fits the event from the start.
templates.blurb: Written the way a caterer runs a first planning call, with the logistics a quote depends on. It asks about the event, the guests, the venue and whether food is served indoors or out, then the service style decides what comes next: a drop-off order skips the staffing questions, while a staffed event is asked about the venue kitchen and what equipment you need to bring. Dietary needs and a ranked list of priorities help you pitch the right menu.

preview.greeting: Hello! Walk us through your event and we'll build a menu and quote around it.
preview.question: What's the occasion?

templates.title: Appointment request
templates.description: Collect the service, the times that work and the context, in a friendly back-and-forth.
templates.metaDescription: Let clients pick a service, share their availability across the week, choose in person or online and tell you what they need, before you confirm a time.
templates.blurb: Instead of a single date box, clients tick the mornings, afternoons and evenings that suit them across the week, so you can offer a slot that works the first time. Anyone unsure which service they need describes the problem instead, and first-time clients are asked how they found you while returning clients skip it.

preview.greeting: Hi there! Let's find a time that works for you.
preview.question: Which service would you like to book?

templates.title: Tattoo consultation
templates.description: Arrive at every tattoo consultation already knowing the idea, the spot and the references.
templates.metaDescription: Gather a client's tattoo idea, style, placement, size, colour and reference images before the consultation, with an age check and cover-up questions built in.
templates.blurb: The questions an artist asks at the start of every consult, answered before it begins. Anyone under 18 is stopped kindly at the start, and cover-ups get their own step asking for a photo of the existing tattoo. Reference images, a flexibility scale and a note on skin or health round it off.

preview.greeting: Hey! Tell us about the tattoo you have in mind.
preview.question: Are you 18 or older?
preview.next: Will this be your first tattoo?

templates.title: Partnership inquiry
templates.description: Hear what a would-be partner offers and whether the timing is right, in one conversation.
templates.metaDescription: Sort real partnership proposals from cold pitches. Each type of partner, from integrations to resellers, is asked the one question that shows it could work.
templates.blurb: A partnerships inbox fills with pitches that were never going to fit. Each kind of partnership is asked the one thing that makes it credible: an integration for which way the API calls go, a reseller for the market it sells into, co-marketing for the size of its audience, an agency for its client base. Proposals looking to move in the next few weeks go to their own ending with a faster reply.

preview.greeting: Thinking of working together? Tell us what you have in mind.
preview.question: Who are we talking to?
preview.next: And which company?

templates.title: Appointment booking
templates.description: Take a booking with the right slot length for the reason.
templates.metaDescription: Take appointment bookings with a date and time, and ask each reason the right questions. First visits give background, urgent requests get a call back.
templates.blurb: A date question with time turned on, so the answer is an appointment rather than a day. First visits are asked what they want to discuss, follow-ups what has changed, and a routine check is a few taps. Anyone who needs to be seen today skips the calendar and lands on an ending that promises a call back.

preview.greeting: Let's find you a time.
preview.question: Your name and the best number to reach you
preview.next: What's the appointment for?

templates.title: Giveaway entry
templates.description: A short, fair entry path that checks eligibility first and records rule acceptance.
templates.metaDescription: Take giveaway entries with an age check up front, one clean record per entrant, how the winner wants the prize, a newsletter opt-in and agreement to the rules.
templates.blurb: Entrants answer the eligibility question before anything else, so anyone under 18 is told kindly and never fills in the rest. Everyone else gets a quick run through contact details, how they would like the prize delivered and a separate newsletter opt-in, so a giveaway entry is never mistaken for marketing consent.

preview.greeting: You're a couple of minutes away from being entered. Let's check you're eligible first.
preview.question: Are you 18 or older?
preview.next: Where should we contact you if you win?

templates.title: Suggestion box
templates.description: Collect improvement ideas with enough context to act on, named or anonymous.
templates.metaDescription: A suggestion box people will actually use: the idea, the problem it solves, who it helps and how much, with an anonymous option and follow-up for named ideas.
templates.blurb: A good suggestion names a problem, not just a wish, so this asks for both. People who raised the idea before are asked what happened to it, which is often the most useful answer you'll get. Anyone who wants to stay anonymous can finish without a name, and named contributors are asked if they'd help make it happen.

preview.greeting: Got an idea that would make things better here? We'd like to hear it, big or small.
preview.question: What is your suggestion about?
preview.answer: How we work day to day

templates.title: Software incident report
templates.description: Record what broke, when, how badly and for whom, in a shape your on-call team can triage.
templates.metaDescription: Log software incidents in one consistent shape: affected service, severity, start time, impact, what was tried and evidence. Critical ones ask for a callback number.
templates.blurb: Written for the person who notices a problem, not the engineer who fixes it, so it asks plain questions and turns them into a triage-ready record. A critical report asks for a number the on-call engineer can ring right away, and an incident that has already stopped is asked how it resolved.

preview.greeting: Something not working? Tell us what you're seeing and we'll get the right person on it.
preview.question: Who is reporting this?
preview.next: Which system, app or service is affected?

templates.title: Client information
templates.description: One record of who your client is, who to bill and who else to keep in the loop.
templates.metaDescription: Gather what you need to start a client project: main contact, legal and billing details, who approves work, which accounts you need and who else to keep informed.
templates.blurb: Built for agencies and freelancers to send once a client signs, so kickoff doesn't start with a week of emails. It records who approves work and which accounts you'll need access to, asks for a separate billing contact only when someone else pays the invoices, and gathers everyone else on the project in one repeating list.

preview.greeting: Welcome aboard! A few details now saves a lot of back and forth later. It takes about five minutes.
preview.question: Who will be our main contact?
preview.next: What is your role or job title?

templates.title: Estimate request
templates.description: Get the job details, photos and timing you need to send a realistic estimate.
templates.metaDescription: Collect what you need to price a job before a site visit: the work, the property, size, photos, timing and budget. Urgent jobs are asked for a number to call.
templates.blurb: For trades and service businesses that lose hours to vague enquiries. It asks what the job is, where, how big and how soon, with room for photos, so you can price it or decide a visit is needed. Urgent jobs are asked for a phone number, and flexible ones skip the start-date question.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell us about the job and we'll come back with an estimate. It takes about three minutes.
preview.question: Who is the estimate for?
preview.next: What kind of job is it?

templates.title: Insurance quote request
templates.description: An insurance enquiry that asks different questions for each type of cover.
templates.metaDescription: Take insurance quote requests that ask the right questions per cover type: home, car, life, health, business or travel, then timing, priorities and contact details.
templates.blurb: One form for every line you sell. The first answer decides the next few questions, so a driver is asked about their car, age and claims while a traveller is asked about their trip, and nobody wades through the rest. Everyone then ranks what matters most to them, which tells your advisers where to start the conversation.

preview.greeting: Looking for cover? Answer a few questions and one of our advisers will come back with a quote.
preview.question: What would you like cover for?

templates.title: Sales call log
templates.description: A quick log reps fill in after each call, with a next step every time.
templates.metaDescription: Log every sales call while it's fresh: who you spoke to, what came up, objections, next step and date. No-answer and lost calls get their own short path.
templates.blurb: Reps fill it in straight after a call, so it has to be quick. The outcome decides the path: a missed call just needs a retry date, a lost deal records why, and a live opportunity captures the summary, objections, lead warmth and an agreed next step with a date.

preview.greeting: Just off a call? Log it now while it's fresh. Two minutes, tops.
preview.question: Who made the call?
preview.next: When was the call?

templates.title: General inquiry
templates.description: Take any question from your website and know who should answer it before you open it.
templates.metaDescription: An inquiry form that takes a subject line and a question, asks for a date when it's about availability or a reference when it's about a booking, then how to reply.
templates.blurb: Reads like an email with the useful parts filled in: a topic, a one-line subject, the question, how soon it needs an answer and how to reply. A question about prices or availability asks for the date in mind, one about an existing booking asks for its reference, and only people who want a call are asked for a number.

preview.greeting: Hi there. Ask us anything and we'll get it to the right person.
preview.question: First, what's your name?
preview.next: What's your inquiry about?

templates.title: Catering contact
templates.description: Hear about the event, the guests and the food before you pick up the phone.
templates.metaDescription: A catering contact form that gets the date, venue, guest count, service style and dietary needs up front, so your first reply can include a real quote.
templates.blurb: Asks what a caterer needs to judge fit and price a job: the occasion, date, venue, headcount, service style and dietary needs. Wedding enquiries are also asked whether they want a tasting, and a budget question stops you proposing a plated dinner to someone who wanted sandwiches.

preview.greeting: Planning an event? Tell us a bit about it and we'll come back with ideas and a quote.
preview.question: What's the occasion?

templates.title: Client consultation
templates.description: Learn the problem and the goal before the first call, not during it.
templates.metaDescription: A client consultation form that collects the problem, what they've tried, the outcome they want, timing and budget, so the first call starts at the real issue.
templates.blurb: Built to prepare a first consultation: what the client needs help with, what they have already tried, what success looks like and what matters most to them. Clients who are only exploring get a friendly close with no call pushed on them, and everyone else picks a day for the conversation.

preview.greeting: Thanks for getting in touch. A few questions now means we can skip the basics on our call.
preview.question: Let's start with who you are.
preview.next: What's your business or organisation called, if you have one?

templates.title: Design project enquiry
templates.description: Get a usable design brief out of every enquiry, not a two-line email.
templates.metaDescription: A contact form for designers: what the client wants made, where it will be used, the look they're after, deadline and budget, plus their brand files or references.
templates.blurb: Asks what a designer needs before quoting: the deliverables, where the work will live, the look the client is after, the deadline and the budget. Clients with an existing brand are asked to upload their files, and those starting fresh are asked for designs they admire instead.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell me about the project and I'll get back to you with next steps.
preview.question: What would you like designed?

templates.title: Photography enquiry
templates.description: Check your calendar and send a quote from the first message.
templates.metaDescription: A photography contact form that asks the type of shoot, date, location and how the photos will be used, with extra questions for weddings and commercial work.
templates.blurb: Starts with the type of shoot, because a wedding and a product shoot need different answers. Couples are asked how much of the day to cover, commercial clients are asked where the images will be used and how many they need, and everyone gives the date, place and style.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell me about the shoot you have in mind and I'll check my availability.
preview.question: What kind of shoot is it?

templates.title: Mobile-friendly contact
templates.description: A contact form built for thumbs: few questions, big choices, no tiny fields.
templates.metaDescription: A short contact form that works on a phone as well as a laptop: tap to pick a reason, type the message, pick how to hear back. Problem reports can add a screenshot.
templates.blurb: Kept short for small screens: one question at a time, tap answers wherever possible, and the message is the only long answer. Someone reporting a problem is asked which device they are on and can attach a screenshot, and only people who want a call are asked for a number.

preview.greeting: Hello! This will only take a minute.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: What can we help with?

templates.title: Contact us
templates.description: A general contact form that sorts the inbox as it fills it.
templates.metaDescription: A contact us form for any website. Buyers pick the next step, support asks for the account, feedback gets a star rating and job seekers can share a profile link.
templates.blurb: The one form every site needs. The topic decides which follow-ups are worth asking: a buyer says whether they want a price, a demo or just an answer, support asks for the account email, feedback starts with a star rating, and job seekers share the role and a profile link. A call back is offered to everyone, with a time slot.

preview.greeting: Hi! What can we help you with?
preview.question: Let's start with your name and email.
preview.next: What's it about?

templates.title: Business contact
templates.description: One contact form for buyers, customers, partners and press, each asked only what their enquiry needs.
templates.metaDescription: A contact form for your business website that asks why someone is getting in touch, then asks only what that kind of enquiry needs so it reaches the right person.
templates.blurb: Built for company websites where buyers, customers, would-be partners and journalists all use the same contact page. It asks which of those the person is first, then branches: a buyer is asked what they need, for how big a team and when, an existing customer for a reference and how urgent it is, a partner what they're proposing, and a journalist for their deadline.

preview.greeting: Hello, and thanks for getting in touch. Pick what your message is about and we'll pass it to the team that handles it.
preview.question: First, who are we talking to?
preview.next: Which company or organisation are you with?

templates.title: Callback request
templates.description: Take callback requests with the number, the reason and a time that suits the caller.
templates.metaDescription: Let people ask for a phone call instead of waiting on hold. Collects the number, the reason, an order reference if there is one and the day and time that suit them.
templates.blurb: Everything your team needs before dialling: who to ask for, the number, what the call is about and when to ring. People calling about an existing order or a bill are asked for its reference, so the agent can pull it up first. Anyone who needs a call today skips the day picker, says when today suits them and lands on an ending that says they are first in line.

preview.greeting: Rather talk it through? Leave your number and we'll call you back.
preview.question: Who should we ask for when we call?
preview.next: What's the best number to reach you on?

templates.title: Client contact
templates.description: Give clients one place to send requests, with the project and context already attached.
templates.metaDescription: A contact form for existing clients that asks which project a message is about, what kind of request it is and how blocking any problem is, so nothing gets lost.
templates.blurb: Built for agencies, freelancers and service teams whose clients message them across email, chat and calls. Every message arrives tied to a project. A problem report asks how badly it is blocking the client and takes screenshots, a billing question asks for the invoice number, and clients who want a call are asked when suits them, with a number only for phone calls.

preview.greeting: Hi. Send us anything about your project here and it'll reach the right person on the team.
preview.question: Your name and email
preview.next: Which company are you with?

templates.title: Sales inquiry
templates.description: Learn what a buyer needs and how soon, and fast-track the ones ready to buy now.
templates.metaDescription: Find out what a buyer wants, how much, by when and who decides. Buyers ready this month are asked for a number to call; everyone else gets a reply by email.
templates.blurb: Asks the things a salesperson needs before replying: what the buyer is after, rough quantity, budget position and timing. Anyone who wants to start this month is asked for a phone number and a good time, and lands on an ending that promises a call. Everyone else is asked who makes the decision.

preview.greeting: Thanks for your interest. A few questions and we'll come back with something useful, not a brochure.
preview.question: Who should we reply to?
preview.next: Which company are you buying for?

templates.title: Complaint form
templates.description: Record what happened, its impact and the outcome the person wants, in their own words.
templates.metaDescription: Let people report what went wrong, when, how it affected them and what would put it right. Safety concerns get their own follow-up, and past contact is recorded.
templates.blurb: A complaint form that takes the person seriously. It records what happened and when, how serious it was and what they want done. A safety concern gets its own follow-up, anyone who has complained before is asked who they spoke to, and someone who only wants it on record gets an ending that says it has been.

preview.greeting: We're sorry something went wrong. Tell us what happened and we'll look into it properly.
preview.question: Your name and email, so we can reply
preview.next: What is your complaint about?

templates.title: Customer contact
templates.description: Let customers ask a question and include the order or product it's about.
templates.metaDescription: A contact form for shop and service customers. Order questions ask for the order number and photos, product questions ask which one, and a phone number is optional.
templates.blurb: Customers rarely know what your team needs from them, so this form asks for them. A question about an order asks for the order number and lets them add photos. A question before buying asks which product it is. A phone number is only requested from customers who want a call.

preview.greeting: Hi! What can we help you with today?
preview.question: Your name and email
preview.next: What's your question about?

templates.title: Customer profile
templates.description: Learn who a customer is, what they want from you and how they like to be contacted.
templates.metaDescription: Build a useful record of each customer: what they want from you, what matters most, how they like to be contacted and whether they're happy to hear about offers.
templates.blurb: A profile that goes further than name and address. Customers rank what matters most to them, say what they want help with and choose how you may contact them, with marketing consent asked separately and clearly. Business customers get a few extra questions about their company.

preview.greeting: Welcome! A few questions so we can look after you properly.
preview.question: Your contact details
preview.next: Are you buying for yourself or for a business?

templates.title: Client onboarding
templates.description: Everything you need from a new client before kickoff, asked in the order a good project lead would.
templates.metaDescription: Start a new client project with the goals, contacts, sign-off process, files and first priority in one place, so kickoff is spent on the work, not admin.
templates.blurb: Collects the brief, the contacts, how the client likes to work and the materials you need before day one. Clients who sign off as a group are asked who else approves the work, and anyone with nothing ready yet skips the upload step instead of being asked for files they don't have.

preview.greeting: Welcome aboard! A few questions now will save us a lot of back and forth later.
preview.question: Who will be our main point of contact?
preview.next: What's your company or brand called?

templates.title: Bug report
templates.description: Reproducible bug reports instead of "it's broken".
templates.metaDescription: Get bug reports your engineers can reproduce: steps, expected and actual results, and the right details for browser, mobile app or API problems.
templates.blurb: Asks for the three things an engineer needs and a reporter often forgets: what they expected, what happened, and the exact steps between. Where the bug happened decides what comes next (a browser is asked about the console, a phone about its model and app version, an API call about the status code), and anyone who can't work at all lands on an urgent ending.

preview.greeting: Sorry something's broken. Let's get the details down so we can fix it.
preview.question: In one line, what went wrong?
preview.next: What steps lead to it? Number them if you can.

templates.title: Customer complaint
templates.description: For shops and service businesses: a complaint about a purchase, with the order and the fix the customer wants.
templates.metaDescription: Hear a complaint about an order, delivery or visit in full: where they bought, the order number, what went wrong, the fix they want and whether they'd come back.
templates.blurb: Built around a purchase rather than a general grievance. It asks where the customer bought, so a store visit is asked which branch while an online order goes straight to the order number, then lets them tick every problem at once. It closes by asking whether they'd buy again if it were put right, and customers who want a phone call get a number question and an ending that says so.

preview.greeting: Sorry your order didn't go the way it should. Tell us what happened and we'll work out how to put it right.
preview.question: First, your name and the email you used when you bought
preview.next: Where did you buy from us?

templates.title: Customer inquiry
templates.description: Questions from shoppers and customers, each arriving with the product or order it's about.
templates.metaDescription: Answer shoppers' questions about products, delivery, orders and returns, with the product link or order number attached and a note of who is ready to buy.
templates.blurb: Made for businesses that sell something: each topic asks for the one detail your team would otherwise reply to ask for. A product question asks which product and how close the person is to buying, a delivery question asks where it's going, and an order, return or account question asks for the order number. Only people who want a call are asked for a phone number.

preview.greeting: Hi! Ask us anything about our products or your order.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: And your email address?

templates.title: Service request
templates.description: One form for every kind of service request, with the right follow-up questions for each.
templates.metaDescription: Take repair, return, installation, account change and cancellation requests in one form that asks each type of request only the details it needs.
templates.blurb: The request type decides what is asked next. A repair is asked which product and what's wrong, an installation visit is asked what it's for, the address, the earliest date and any access notes, and a cancellation is asked why, so every request arrives ready to act on.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell us what you need and we'll get the right person on it.
preview.question: Who is the request for?
preview.next: Your customer, order or account number

templates.title: Missing FAQ question
templates.description: Collect the questions your FAQ doesn't answer yet, in your customers' own words.
templates.metaDescription: Find the gaps in your help content: collect the questions people couldn't find answered, in their own words, with where they looked and how stuck they are.
templates.blurb: Put it at the bottom of your help pages to catch the questions they miss. It records where people looked first and how much the gap is holding them up, asks what was confusing when an answer existed but didn't help, and only asks for an email when someone wants a personal reply.

preview.greeting: Couldn't find what you were looking for? Ask here and we'll use it to improve our answers.
preview.question: What question couldn't you find an answer to?
preview.next: Which area is it about?

templates.title: Data deletion request
templates.description: A clear route for right-to-erasure requests, with enough detail to find the records.
templates.metaDescription: Let people ask you to erase their personal data under GDPR, with the details you need to find their records and a declaration before you act.
templates.blurb: Collects who is asking, how they know you and what they want erased, then asks for a signed-off declaration before anything is deleted. People who only want to stop marketing emails get their own ending, and anyone asking on someone else's behalf is asked for their own contact details and proof they can act.

preview.greeting: You can ask us to delete the personal data we hold about you. It only takes a few minutes.
preview.question: What's your full name?
preview.next: Which email address do we know you by?

templates.title: Refund request
templates.description: Refund requests with the evidence your team needs, collected once.
templates.metaDescription: Handle refund requests with the order reference, reason and evidence up front: photos for damage, tracking for missing parcels, statements for double charges.
templates.blurb: Order reference, reason and preferred outcome, asked once so nobody has to email back for them. A damaged item is asked for photos, a missing parcel for its tracking status, and a double charge goes straight to finance with its own ending. The reason list also becomes a running count of why people ask for their money back.

preview.greeting: Let's sort this out. First, a few details about the order.
preview.question: Which email did you use for the order?
preview.next: Your order or invoice number

templates.title: Support ticket
templates.description: Route requests to the right queue, with the details that queue needs.
templates.metaDescription: A support ticket form that sorts each request by category, asks the details that queue needs, and records what the customer has already tried.
templates.blurb: Asking for the category up front sends each ticket to the right person without a triage pass, and each category asks its own questions: billing gets an invoice number, login gets the exact error, a how-to question gets asked about the goal instead of the button. Blocking tickets get their own ending so the customer knows they were flagged.

preview.greeting: How can we help? Tell us what's going on.
preview.question: What's the email on your account?
preview.next: What's this about?

templates.title: Product onboarding
templates.description: Find out what a new customer needs to get started, before they get lost.
templates.metaDescription: Learn what each new customer wants from your product, who will use it and what to set up first, then offer a walkthrough call to those who want one.
templates.blurb: Asks new customers for their goal, their team and what they want to set up first, so your welcome can be about their job instead of a generic tour. People switching from another tool are asked what they're leaving and whether data needs to come across, and anyone who wants a walkthrough is asked for a number and a date.

preview.greeting: Welcome! Tell us a little about what you're here to do and we'll help you get started.
preview.question: What's your name and email?
preview.next: Which company or team are you with?

templates.title: Product evaluation
templates.description: Score a product on the job it has to do, and find out exactly where it falls short.
templates.metaDescription: Rate a product against clear criteria: usefulness, ease of use, quality and value. Reviewers who find gaps say what is missing and whether it is a dealbreaker.
templates.blurb: Starts from the job the product was used for, then scores it on the same criteria for every reviewer so products can be compared fairly. If it falls even slightly short, the form asks what is missing and whether that rules it out, instead of asking for praise it has not earned.

preview.greeting: Thanks for trying the product. A few questions on how it held up in real use.
preview.question: Which product are you evaluating?
preview.next: What did you use it for?

templates.title: Software evaluation
templates.description: Test software on real work and get a recommendation each reviewer can explain.
templates.metaDescription: Have reviewers score software on the tasks your team really does: requirements met, ease of use, limitations and a clear recommendation with their reasons.
templates.blurb: Built for a team trial: each reviewer records what they tested, how the tool met each requirement and what broke. Security concerns get their own follow-up, and the final recommendation branches so a conditional yes says what the conditions are and a no says why.

preview.greeting: You've had time with the tool. Let's capture what you found while it's fresh.
preview.question: Which software are you evaluating?
preview.next: Which best describes your part in this evaluation?

templates.title: Self evaluation
templates.description: A reflective self-review that gives the review conversation real examples to work from.
templates.metaDescription: Help employees prepare for a performance review: wins with real examples, progress on goals, strengths, challenges and the support they need next period.
templates.blurb: Asks for evidence rather than adjectives: a win with an example, how goals actually went and a challenge handled. Missed goals and a heavy workload each get a follow-up question, so the manager walks into the review knowing what got in the way.

preview.greeting: This is your space to reflect before your review. Honest beats polished.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: What's your role, and which team are you on?

templates.title: Online event registration
templates.description: Sign people up for the sessions they want and send the right access details to each.
templates.metaDescription: Register attendees for a virtual conference, online workshop or summit: session choices, timezone, access needs and questions for the speakers in advance.
templates.blurb: Built for an online event with several sessions: attendees pick the ones they want, so you know which rooms will fill. Anyone who chooses the hands-on workshop is asked what device they will use and how experienced they are, since that session needs more from them than watching.

preview.greeting: Welcome! Let's get you registered and tell you where to join.
preview.question: Who's registering?
preview.next: Which organisation are you with, if any?

templates.title: Event volunteer signup
templates.description: Find out who can help, when, and with what, before you draw up the rota.
templates.metaDescription: Recruit volunteers for your event: shifts they can cover, roles ranked by preference, useful skills, an emergency contact and agreement to the volunteer code.
templates.blurb: Collects exactly what you need to build a volunteer rota: available shifts, a ranking of preferred roles, and skills like first aid that change where someone is most useful. First aiders are asked when their certificate runs out, so you only roster ones who are current on the day. Volunteers under 18 give a parent or guardian contact, and everyone agrees to the volunteer code at the end.

preview.greeting: Thanks for offering to help! This takes a few minutes and helps us put you in the right place.
preview.question: How can we reach you?
preview.next: Are you 18 or over?

templates.title: Hackathon registration
templates.description: Register hackers, sort out teams, and know who needs food, a T-shirt or a teammate.
templates.metaDescription: Register hackathon participants: background, skills, team status, track interest, T-shirt size and dietary needs. Solo hackers can ask to be matched with a team.
templates.blurb: Covers what organisers actually need before the weekend: skills, experience, which track people want and whether they already have a team. Anyone looking for teammates says what they can bring and what they need, so matching is quick, and everyone agrees to the code of conduct before they finish.

preview.greeting: Ready to build something? Let's get you registered for the hackathon.
preview.question: Who's hacking?
preview.next: Which best describes you right now?

templates.title: Webinar registration
templates.description: Register attendees, and ask the ones who can't join live what would have helped.
templates.metaDescription: Register webinar attendees and collect their questions in advance. People who can't join live get the recording and tell you what kept them away.
templates.blurb: The best webinar Q&A is written before the webinar starts. This asks what attendees want covered, and splits the people joining live from the ones who only want the recording, because those two get different emails afterwards and each reaches its own ending that says so.

preview.greeting: Save your seat. It takes about a minute.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: Where should we send the joining link?

templates.title: Workshop registration
templates.description: Sign people up and check they're ready for the day.
templates.metaDescription: Sign people up for a hands-on workshop and check they're ready: session choice, experience level, setup and goals. Beginners get extra prep, experts don't.
templates.blurb: A hands-on workshop goes badly when half the room hasn't installed anything. This asks about experience and setup so the right prep email goes to the right people: beginners are asked what they have tried and offered pre-reading, while experienced attendees say what they want to go deep on.

preview.greeting: Let's get you registered. A few details and you're set.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: What email should the prep instructions go to?

templates.title: Event signup
templates.description: A quick signup that tells you who is coming, how, and what they want from the day.
templates.metaDescription: Let guests sign up for your event in a minute: contact details, in person or online, group size, access needs and the parts of the programme they care about.
templates.blurb: Asks early whether someone is coming in person or joining online, then only asks what matters for that choice: group size and access needs for the venue, a timezone for the stream. Everyone finishes by picking the parts of the programme they are most interested in, which helps you plan rooms and reminders.

preview.greeting: Glad you're interested! Let's get you on the list. It takes about a minute.
preview.question: Who should we put on the list?
preview.next: How are you planning to join?

templates.title: Event RSVP
templates.description: Collect RSVPs with plus-ones, dietary notes and travel.
templates.metaDescription: Collect RSVPs for a party, wedding or celebration: plus-ones, guest names, dietary needs and travel. Guests who can't come are thanked and let go in seconds.
templates.blurb: Everything the caterer and the door list need, in the order a guest thinks about it, and nothing else. Someone who can't come is asked one kind question and reaches their own ending in seconds; someone who is coming is walked through guests, food and arrival. Guest names are only asked for when someone brings guests, and the kitchen follow-up only appears if a dietary need needs explaining.

preview.greeting: You're invited! 🎉 Let us know if you can make it.
preview.question: What's your full name?
preview.next: What email should we send the details to nearer the time?

templates.title: Website design feedback
templates.description: Structured comments on a page design, ranked by what should change first.
templates.metaDescription: Get usable feedback on a website design: first impression, readability, navigation and the changes that matter most, with a call offered to talk them over.
templates.blurb: Built for design reviews that usually end in a messy email thread. Reviewers who can't tell what the page is for are asked what confused them, everyone ranks what should change first, and anyone who wants to talk it through leaves an email and lands on their own ending.

preview.greeting: Thanks for looking over the new design. A few quick questions and your comments will be in one tidy place.
preview.question: Which page are you reviewing?
preview.next: Which best describes you?

templates.title: Call review
templates.description: A consistent call review that turns each score into coaching or recognition.
templates.metaDescription: Score a customer call the same way every time: greeting, listening, accuracy, tone and resolution, with a coaching plan for weak calls and praise for strong ones.
templates.blurb: A call review for team leads and QA reviewers that sticks to what can be heard on the recording. A low overall score opens a short coaching plan with a follow-up date, a strong one asks what the agent did well and whether the call belongs in training, and unresolved calls are asked what got in the way.

preview.greeting: Let's review a call. Have the recording or transcript open while you go.
preview.question: Which agent took the call?
preview.next: When was the call?

templates.title: Restaurant feedback
templates.description: Hear what diners thought of the meal, and reach the unhappy ones quickly.
templates.metaDescription: Ask diners about the food, service and value after a visit. Unhappy guests can ask the manager to get in touch, and happy ones tell you the dish they'd order again.
templates.blurb: A short post-visit form that works for dine-in, takeaway and delivery. Guests who rate the visit three stars or less are asked what went wrong and can leave their details for the manager, while happy guests name the dish they'd come back for, which is exactly what you want to feature.

preview.greeting: Thanks for eating with us. How was it? This takes about a minute.
preview.question: How did you eat with us?

templates.title: Store visit feedback
templates.description: What shoppers found, who helped and how checkout went, from the shop floor.
templates.metaDescription: Find out how a shop visit went: finding products, help from staff and the wait at checkout. Shoppers who leave empty-handed say what they came for.
templates.blurb: A store feedback form that covers the three places a visit goes wrong: finding the product, getting help and paying. Shoppers who couldn't find what they came for are asked what it was, and anyone who scores the visit low can ask the store manager to follow up.

preview.greeting: Thanks for shopping with us. Tell us how your visit went, it takes about a minute.
preview.question: Which store did you visit?
preview.next: What brought you in today?

templates.title: Coaching feedback
templates.description: Check in with coaching clients on progress, and shape the next session around it.
templates.metaDescription: Ask coaching clients what's working: progress on their goal, which exercises help and what would make the next session more useful. Promoters are asked for a quote.
templates.blurb: A mid-programme check-in for coaches, not an end-of-course survey. Clients who say coaching isn't giving them what they hoped for are asked what's missing and whether to talk before the next session, and those who would strongly recommend you are asked for a testimonial.

preview.greeting: Thanks for taking a few minutes. Your answers shape how we spend our next sessions.
preview.question: What's your first name?
preview.next: What's the main goal you're working on with me?

templates.title: Presentation feedback
templates.description: Find out whether your talk landed, in the audience's own words.
templates.metaDescription: Get honest comments after a talk: was the message clear, the structure easy to follow and the pace right? Listeners also restate the main point in their own words.
templates.blurb: Starts with the most honest test of a talk: asking the listener to sum up the main point in a sentence. It then rates structure, examples, slides and pace, and asks lower scorers what would have helped most and higher scorers what worked best.

preview.greeting: Thanks for listening. A couple of minutes of honest feedback helps the next talk a lot.
preview.question: Which talk or session are you giving feedback on?
preview.next: How well did you know the topic beforehand?

templates.title: Release feedback
templates.description: Hear how a new release changed people's work, and catch what broke.
templates.metaDescription: Learn how a release landed with users: whether they noticed the changes, what got easier or harder, what's broken and what needs explaining better.
templates.blurb: A post-release form that treats three kinds of user differently. People who used the new features rate the change, people who noticed but didn't try them say why, and people who missed it entirely say where they'd expect to hear. Anyone who hit a bug describes it, rates how badly it hurts and can attach a screenshot.

preview.greeting: We've just shipped an update. Tell us how it's going for you, it takes about two minutes.
preview.question: Which version are you using, if you know?
preview.next: How often do you use the product?

templates.title: Client feedback
templates.description: Hear how the project really went, and route happy and unhappy clients differently.
templates.metaDescription: Ask clients how a project went: the result, the communication and what to change next time. Happy clients get a testimonial ask, unhappy ones a follow-up.
templates.blurb: A short debrief to send when a project wraps. The overall score decides the next question: a client who loved the work is asked for a quote you can publish, and one who didn't is asked what went wrong and whether they want a call about it.

preview.greeting: Thanks for working with us. Got two minutes to tell us how it went?
preview.question: Which project are you reviewing?
preview.next: Overall, how happy are you with the result?

templates.title: Music submission
templates.description: Collect tracks and artist details in one consistent format for review.
templates.metaDescription: Receive tracks from artists in one consistent format: the audio, genre, release status, bio and links, plus live setup details when they want a booking.
templates.blurb: For playlists, venues, labels and events that are tired of links scattered across inboxes. Artists upload the track and describe it the same way every time, released tracks add a streaming link, upcoming ones give a release date, and anyone asking for a live slot describes their setup.

preview.greeting: Thanks for sending us your music. This takes about five minutes, and every track gets listened to.
preview.question: What's your artist or band name?
preview.next: Who should we contact about this submission?

templates.title: Photo contest entry
templates.description: Take contest entries with everything the judges need, and screen out ineligible ones.
templates.metaDescription: Take photography competition entries with the image, category, title and the story behind the shot. Under-18s add a guardian, and composites are screened out.
templates.blurb: Collects the photo along with what judges actually look at: the category, a title, where and when it was taken and the story behind it. Entrants under 18 give a parent or guardian's details, and anyone who has composited their image is told politely before they upload that it isn't eligible.

preview.greeting: Welcome to the photo contest. Entering takes about three minutes. Have your photo ready.
preview.question: Who's entering?
preview.next: How old are you?

templates.title: Project submission
templates.description: Take proposals and finished projects in one consistent format for review.
templates.metaDescription: Receive project proposals and finished work in one place: title, summary, team, files and links. Proposals give a start date and budget, finished work its results.
templates.blurb: Works for course projects, grant rounds, hackathons and internal pitches. Solo and team submissions are handled separately, proposals are asked for a start date and budget, and completed work is asked what it achieved, so reviewers get what they need for each without one long form.

preview.greeting: Ready to submit your project? This takes about five minutes. Have your files and links to hand.
preview.question: Who's submitting?
preview.next: What's the project called?

templates.title: Art submission
templates.description: Receive artwork and the context a curator or editor needs to review it.
templates.metaDescription: Collect artwork for a show, open call or publication: images of the work, medium, size, year and statement, with a price asked only when the piece is for sale.
templates.blurb: An open call form for galleries, exhibitions and publications. Artists upload images of the work and give the details a curator needs to picture it in the room: medium, size, year and an artist statement. The asking price is only asked when the work is for sale, and three-dimensional work gets a question about handling.

preview.greeting: Thanks for submitting your work. This takes about five minutes. Have images of the piece ready.
preview.question: Who's the artist?
preview.next: Your website or online portfolio, if you have one

templates.title: Model application
templates.description: Collect photos, experience and availability from aspiring and working models.
templates.metaDescription: Take modelling applications in one consistent format: the work someone does, recent photos, a portfolio link and availability. Under-18s get a guardian step.
templates.blurb: Built for agencies and casting teams who are tired of applications arriving as DMs with one blurry photo. It asks for the kind of work first, then recent unretouched shots and a portfolio. Applicants under 18 are routed to a parent or guardian contact before they continue, and people with no experience are asked what draws them in rather than for credits they do not have.

preview.greeting: Thanks for your interest in working with us. This takes about four minutes, and it helps to have two or three recent photos on your phone.
preview.question: First, who are we talking to?
preview.next: How old are you?

templates.title: Job application
templates.description: Screen candidates, and ask each discipline its own questions.
templates.metaDescription: Screen candidates with one application form for every team: engineers share code, designers a portfolio, sales their numbers. Everyone gets the same core questions.
templates.blurb: Everything a first-pass review needs and nothing it doesn't. The role someone picks decides what they are asked next: engineers get a code sample question, designers a portfolio walkthrough, sales their deal sizes. One form serves five hiring managers, and anyone without the right to work where the role is based is told straight away rather than after an interview.

preview.greeting: Glad you're interested in joining us. This takes a few minutes, and you can attach your CV near the end.
preview.question: Let's start with your details
preview.next: Where are you based?

templates.title: Contact data capture
templates.description: One tidy contact record per person, whether they are new or updating details you hold.
templates.metaDescription: Build a clean contact record for every person: name, organisation, sector, address, preferred channel and consent, plus a short path for people updating old details.
templates.blurb: Made for keeping a contact list you can trust, not just catching a message. New contacts give a full record in fixed formats, while existing contacts say which email you had and what changed, so you can merge instead of duplicating. A phone number is asked only of people who prefer calls.

preview.greeting: Hi. This takes about two minutes and keeps the details we hold for you accurate.
preview.question: Are you new to us, or updating details we already have?

templates.title: Hotel group and event enquiry
templates.description: Group stays, meetings and weddings, each asked the details that decide availability.
templates.metaDescription: Collect group stay, meeting and wedding enquiries with dates, numbers, room needs and priorities, and spot the guests ready to book so sales can call them first.
templates.blurb: Built for a hotel sales team handling group business. A group stay goes straight to room counts, while meetings and weddings are asked about headcount, layout and event space first. Guests who say they are ready to book land on their own ending, so they can be called before the rest.

preview.greeting: Planning a group stay or an event with us? Tell us what you have in mind and we'll check availability.
preview.question: What is your arrival date, or the date the event starts?
preview.next: How many nights?

templates.title: Prospective client
templates.description: Understand a potential client's need, history and timing before you talk.
templates.metaDescription: Learn a prospective client's goal, what they have tried, their timing and budget before the first call, and let people who prefer email skip the phone questions.
templates.blurb: Written for consultants, coaches and small agencies who want the first conversation to be useful. People who have tried to fix the problem before are asked what happened, and anyone who would rather not talk on the phone gets a reply by email instead of a call request.

preview.greeting: Thanks for thinking of us. A few questions now means our first conversation can get straight to the useful part.
preview.question: Let's start with your name and email.
preview.next: Which company or project is this for?

templates.title: Website design quote
templates.description: Gather the pages, features and content a web design quote depends on.
templates.metaDescription: Scope a website project before you price it: goal, pages, features, content, brand files and launch date, with extra questions for redesigns and online shops.
templates.blurb: Asks the questions that actually move a website price. A redesign is asked for the current site and what is wrong with it, an online shop is asked how many products it will sell, and everyone is asked about pages, features and whether the content is ready, which is where most projects slip.

preview.greeting: Thinking about a new website? Tell us about the project and we'll come back with a proposal.
preview.question: Who are we putting the quote together for?
preview.next: Tell us about your business in a sentence or two.

templates.title: Demo request
templates.description: Take a demo request and learn exactly what to show before the call.
templates.metaDescription: Qualify demo requests by company size, role and timeline, and learn what each prospect wants to see, whether integrations, security or a migration.
templates.blurb: Half of a good demo is knowing what to skip. This asks what the prospect most wants to see, and each answer opens the one follow-up that makes the demo specific: which tools it must connect to, which compliance rules apply, or what they are moving off. Prospects who want to go live this month land on their own ending so sales can call them first.

preview.greeting: Let's set up your demo. Two minutes of questions so we can show you what matters and skip what doesn't.
preview.question: Who should we be speaking to?
preview.next: Which company are you with?

templates.title: Content download
templates.description: Gate a guide without making it feel like a toll booth.
templates.metaDescription: Gate an ebook, guide or report with a short form. Everyone gets the download fast, and only readers researching a purchase are asked if they want a conversation.
templates.blurb: Every extra field costs downloads, so the essentials come first and the rest depends on why someone came. Readers researching a purchase are asked about timing and whether they want to talk, which sends them to their own ending, while people who are just learning get their guide and are left alone.

preview.greeting: Your guide is nearly ready. Tell us where to send it.
preview.question: What's your work email?
preview.next: And your first name?

templates.title: Lead capture
templates.description: Qualify visitors, and send the big ones to sales and the rest to a trial.
templates.metaDescription: Capture leads with the context sales needs: who they are, what they want solved and how soon. Larger teams ready to buy go to sales, the rest to a trial.
templates.blurb: Ask who they are and what they are trying to solve before you ask for a meeting. Team size decides the middle of the conversation: larger teams are asked about the decision and their requirements, smaller ones where they are up to. Timeline is the last question and decides the ending, so a team buying this quarter is handed to sales and everyone else is pointed at a trial they can start today.

preview.greeting: Hi! Interested in what we do? A few quick questions and we'll point you to the right next step.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: What's your work email?

templates.title: Lead qualification
templates.description: Find out goal, fit, budget, timing and buying process before the first call.
templates.metaDescription: Qualify leads before the first call: their goal, fit, budget, timing and who signs off. Buyers with a date get a call and early researchers a softer ending.
templates.blurb: The questions a good sales rep asks in the first ten minutes, answered before the call is booked. Someone researching on behalf of another person is asked who actually decides. Anyone with a date in mind is promised a call within a business day, while people who are only exploring get a friendly nurture ending instead of a pushy follow-up.

preview.greeting: Thanks for reaching out. A few questions now means our first conversation can be about you, not a questionnaire.
preview.question: Who should we speak to?
preview.next: Which company are you with?

templates.title: Customer lead
templates.description: Turn an interested visitor into a conversation, with the context to reply well.
templates.metaDescription: A short customer lead form for small businesses: what the person needs, their rough budget and timing, and how they'd like you to get back to them.
templates.blurb: For the enquiry button on a small business website. It asks what someone needs in their own words, then the practical details that shape a good first reply: budget range, timing and the way they want to be contacted. People who would rather have a call are asked for a number and a good time, and nobody else is.

preview.greeting: Hi there! Tell us a little about what you're after and we'll come back to you with something useful.
preview.question: What's your name?
preview.next: What email should we reply to?

templates.title: Free giveaway claim
templates.description: Let people claim a free item and choose how they receive it, one per person.
templates.metaDescription: Hand out free samples, books or merch while stock lasts: one claim per person, then posted, collected or sent digitally, with newsletter consent kept separate.
templates.blurb: For giveaways where everyone who asks gets something, not a prize draw: free samples, a book, a starter kit or event merch. Repeat claimers are stopped politely before they give an address, and the delivery choice decides the rest, so only people who want it posted are asked where they live. It closes by asking what they want to hear about, which turns a freebie into a lead you can follow up.

preview.greeting: Thanks for claiming your free gift! Tell us who you are and how you'd like to receive it, and we'll take care of the rest.
preview.question: Who's claiming?
preview.next: Have you claimed this giveaway from us before?

templates.title: KYC form
templates.description: Gather identity, address and ownership details for an initial customer review.
templates.metaDescription: Collect details for an initial know your customer review from individuals or businesses: identity, address, documents and source of funds, each with a reason.
templates.blurb: Individuals and businesses answer different questions, so a sole customer is never asked for a registration number and a company is asked who owns it. Each request says why it is needed, which makes people more willing to share. Anyone who says they hold a public position gets one extra question, and nobody else sees it.

preview.greeting: Before we can open your account we need to confirm a few details about you. It takes about five minutes, and it helps to have an ID and a recent bill or bank statement nearby.
preview.question: Let's start with your contact details
preview.next: Are you applying as an individual or on behalf of a business?

templates.title: Product recommendation
templates.description: Learn what a shopper needs so your team can suggest the right product.
templates.metaDescription: Let shoppers tell you what they need: how they'll use it, what matters most, their budget and deadline, so your team can reply with a recommendation that fits.
templates.blurb: The questions a good shop assistant asks, in the order they ask them. Intended use comes first, then a ranking of what matters most, so a tie between two products is easy to break. Gift buyers are asked who the gift is for and by when, and people who want a call rather than an email give a number, while everyone else skips it.

preview.greeting: Not sure what to choose? Answer a few questions and one of our team will send you a personal recommendation.
preview.question: What are you looking for?
preview.next: Who is it for?

templates.title: New client intake
templates.description: Everything you need before the first client session, asked in the right order.
templates.metaDescription: Collect a new client's details, background and goals before the first session. Projects, retainers and second opinions each get their own follow-up questions.
templates.blurb: Replaces the intake PDF nobody fills in. What someone is here for decides what they are asked next: a one-off project gets scope, deadline and budget, an ongoing engagement gets cadence and decision-makers, and a second opinion gets asked what was said the first time. Everyone ends on the same background, goals and terms.

preview.greeting: Welcome! A few questions now means we can spend our first session on the real work.
preview.question: First, your details
preview.next: Which organisation are you with, if any?

templates.title: Client profile
templates.description: A reference record of a client's business, customers, market and priorities.
templates.metaDescription: Build a lasting record of each client: what they sell, their best customers, competitors, priorities and who signs off. The approver is asked for only when needed.
templates.blurb: A profile you keep coming back to across projects, not a one-off intake. It records what the business sells, who its best customers are, who it competes with and how it ranks its priorities this year. If the person filling it in isn't the one who signs off, the form asks who is.

preview.greeting: Hi! We'd like to get to know your business properly. This takes about four minutes.
preview.question: Who are we talking to?
preview.next: What's your role there?

templates.title: Demo feedback
templates.description: Hear what landed in the demo, what didn't, and what the buyer wants next.
templates.metaDescription: Find out if your product demo answered the buyer's questions, what was missing and what they want next. Poor fits explain why; keen buyers share their timeline.
templates.blurb: Sent right after a sales demo, it rates the session, pins down what went unanswered and asks what should happen next. Buyers who want a technical deep dive are asked what to cover, keen buyers share their timeline and who else decides, and anyone who isn't a fit is asked why and gets a polite ending of their own.

preview.greeting: Thanks for joining the demo today. Could you spare two minutes to tell us how it went?
preview.question: Your name and work email
preview.next: Which company are you with?

templates.title: Design consultation
templates.description: Everything a designer needs to walk into the first meeting with ideas.
templates.metaDescription: Prepare for a design consultation with the client's goal, audience, what prompted the project and what they want from the meeting. Existing brands say what stays.
templates.blurb: Built for the meeting before any quote: it asks what prompted the project, what the design has to achieve, who it is for and what the client most wants to leave the consultation with. Clients with an existing brand explain what isn't working and what has to stay, and can upload their files; new brands skip straight to references.

preview.greeting: Hi! Tell us about your project and we'll come to the consultation with some ideas already.
preview.question: Your name and email
preview.next: What's the business or brand called?

templates.title: Store registration
templates.description: One sign-up for customers, trade buyers and sellers, each asked what fits.
templates.metaDescription: Register shoppers, wholesale buyers and brands who want to sell through your store with one form. Each type gets its own questions and its own next steps.
templates.blurb: Stores usually run three sign-ups for three kinds of people. This one asks up front who is registering and branches: shoppers pick their interests, wholesale buyers give business and volume details for approval, and brands describe what they would like to list. Each group finishes on an ending that says what happens next for them.

preview.greeting: Welcome! Let's get you registered. First, a couple of quick details.
preview.question: Your name, email and phone
preview.next: How would you like to register?

templates.title: Event planning consultation
templates.description: The occasion, numbers, venue and priorities, gathered before the first meeting.
templates.metaDescription: Collect the occasion, date, guest count, venue, budget and priorities before an event planning consultation. Clients without a venue describe what they want.
templates.blurb: Built for planners who want the first meeting to be about ideas, not logistics. It covers the occasion, date, guest count, budget and services, then asks the client to rank what matters most. Clients who already have a venue name it; clients who don't describe the area and the kind of place they have in mind.

preview.greeting: Planning something? Tell us about the event and we'll come to the consultation with ideas ready.
preview.question: Your name, email and phone
preview.next: What's the occasion?

templates.title: Marketing brief
templates.description: A campaign brief that covers the goal, audience, message, channels and deadline.
templates.metaDescription: Collect the goal, audience, key message, channels, deliverables, budget and deadline for a campaign in one brief. Brands without guidelines describe their tone.
templates.blurb: Written for agencies and in-house teams who are tired of briefs that arrive as a one-line email. It asks for the goal and how success will be measured, the audience and message, channels and deliverables, then budget and dates. Teams with brand guidelines upload them; teams without describe the tone they want.

preview.greeting: Let's get the campaign brief down. It takes about five minutes and saves a lot of back and forth.

preview.greeting: Would you say a few words about working with us? It really helps.

An age check at the start stops anyone under 16 with a friendly ending instead of an error.

templates.title: Gym membership

Members who are moving away skip the offer entirely.

preview.greeting: Sorry to see you go. This takes about a minute, and the feedback questions at the end are optional.

preview.greeting: Glad you want to join us. A few questions and we'll take it from there.
preview.question: Your name, email and phone

Access notes and photos come before the timing question, so an emergency order still reaches the on-call team with everything they need.

templates.blurb: Asks for everything the kitchen and the driver need: the menu, the headcount, the serving time and the dietary counts. Anyone who mentions a severe allergy is asked for the details, and customers collecting from you skip the venue and on-site contact questions entirely.

preview.greeting: Hello! Let's get your catering order down. Have your guest numbers and menu choice to hand.
preview.question: Who's placing the order?
